items.prompt: What is the earliest prefix length at which a self-inclusive value can strictly exceed three population standard deviations?

options.why: The squared self-inclusive z-score is at most n-1; exceeding 9 requires n>10.

options.text: 2 observations if the spike is large enough.
options.why: The self-inclusive standardized score bound depends on n, not the absolute scale of the spike.
At n=10 the maximum squared score is 9, and strict inequality excludes equality.

options.text: Never, because including x always makes its deviation zero.
options.why: Its deviation need not be zero. Ten zeros then 1 at n=11 already gives 100>90.
